clinical_scope.population: Adults and young people aged 16 years or older unless otherwise specified by local protocol
excluded_populations: pediatric specialty pathways unless explicitly validated
clinical_scope.intended_use: High-risk candidate retrieval and guideline-based verification for suspected Intracranial Hemorrhage.
clinical_scope.important_boundary: This graph supports clinical reasoning and missed-diagnosis risk reduction; it is not an autonomous diagnostic system.

distinctions.description: Clinical symptoms overlap; urgent brain imaging is required.

relationship_to_other_graphs.boundary_note: This graph is a high-risk intracranial bleeding retrieval graph. Disease-specific subgraphs should be used when ICH/SAH/SDH/EDH subtype is identified.

basic_info.working_definition: Intracranial hemorrhage is bleeding within the cranial vault, including intraparenchymal, subarachnoid, subdural, and epidural compartments.
why_high_risk_for_missed_diagnosis: Can mimic ischemic stroke, migraine, intoxication, seizure, meningitis, or tumor.
Headache may be absent in some hemorrhages; focal deficits can dominate.
Anticoagulant/antiplatelet use, trauma, very high blood pressure, or sudden severe headache are high-risk clues.
Delayed imaging delays reversal, neurosurgical evaluation, and blood-pressure management.
basic_info.time_sensitivity: Requires urgent brain imaging, airway/neurologic monitoring, anticoagulation reversal assessment, blood-pressure management, and neurosurgical/stroke consultation when indicated.

activation_logic.minimum_activation: Acute neurologic deficit, sudden severe headache, seizure/reduced consciousness, anticoagulant/trauma context, or suspected stroke before imaging.

case_features: vomiting or neck stiffness or reduced consciousness
headache without sudden severe onset or neurologic signs

symptom_to_candidate_retrieval.scoring_warning: Weights are for retrieval and explanation only. They are not calibrated probabilities and must not be used as a diagnostic score.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Are sudden severe headache, focal deficit, vomiting, seizure, reduced consciousness, trauma, or anticoagulant use present?
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: Lower priority but do not exclude if stroke syndrome present.
guideline_verification_pathway.if_missing: Cannot assess red flags without history/exam.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Is noncontrast head CT or appropriate MRI available?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Confirm or exclude intracranial blood and subtype.
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: If negative but suspicion persists for SAH/other bleed, follow local pathway.
guideline_verification_pathway.if_missing: Cannot classify stroke type or exclude hemorrhage without imaging.

guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: If no hemorrhage, consider ischemic stroke/mimics.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Are GCS decline, herniation signs, hydrocephalus, mass effect, IVH, or posterior fossa hemorrhage present?
Is the patient taking anticoagulants/antiplatelets or coagulopathic?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Flag for immediate clinician-led reversal assessment.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Is blood pressure or airway/respiratory status requiring urgent management?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Escalate support and BP pathway per local protocol.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Is CTA/MRA/angiography indicated to assess aneurysm, AVM, or vascular lesion?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Identify vascular cause and intervention pathway.
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: Not indicated or negative per local assessment.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Could ischemic stroke, meningitis, encephalitis, seizure, migraine, tumor, or metabolic disorder explain the presentation?
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: Hemorrhage remains primary if imaging supports.

distinguishing_features: Focal deficit overlaps; hemorrhage requires imaging exclusion before reperfusion therapy.
Thunderclap headache, meningism, vomiting, reduced consciousness; may need specific SAH pathway even if broad ICH graph retrieved.
critical_tests_or_data: LP per local pathway when indicated

distinguishing_features: Fever, neck stiffness, altered mental status; CT/LP and empiric therapy decisions may be urgent.
Fever, altered mental status, seizures, focal deficits.
Seizure at onset can be cause or result of hemorrhage; imaging needed.
Headache and neurologic aura can mimic stroke/bleed; sudden worst headache requires hemorrhage exclusion.

final_assessment.safety_statement: Clinical decision support only; urgent clinician assessment is required when a high-risk condition is suspected.

evidence_sources.title: 2022 AHA/ASA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage
evidence_sources.publisher: American Heart Association / American Stroke Association
key_points: Provides recommendations for diagnosis and management of spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage.
Used here for acute hemorrhagic stroke verification, imaging, anticoagulation reversal, blood-pressure management, neurosurgical escalation, and safety constraints.

evidence_sources.title: Signs and Symptoms of Stroke
evidence_sources.publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
key_points: Stroke warning symptoms include sudden weakness/numbness, confusion or speech trouble, visual difficulty, trouble walking/dizziness/loss of balance, and sudden severe headache.
Used for symptom normalization and emergency-recognition nodes.

must_not: Do not make an autonomous definitive diagnosis.
Do not use a single symptom, sign, laboratory result, score, or imaging clue as a standalone rule-in or rule-out criterion.
Do not provide patient-facing reassurance when critical red-flag data are missing.
Do not ignore competing high-risk differential diagnoses.
Do not replace local emergency, specialty, or hospital protocols.
Do not generate medication orders; recommend clinician-led pathway activation instead.
Do not distinguish ischemic from hemorrhagic stroke clinically without brain imaging.
Do not give stroke reassurance after symptom improvement without imaging/context.
must_do: Use this graph for candidate retrieval, missed-diagnosis risk reduction, and guideline-based verification.
Separate supporting evidence, evidence against, and missing critical information.
State whether verification is complete, partial, impossible from available data, or contradicted.
Include differential diagnoses that can mimic the condition.
Trace guideline-dependent claims to evidence IDs.
Mark output as clinical decision support requiring qualified clinician review.
Always state imaging status and anticoagulation status.
Always assess neurologic deterioration and neurosurgical red flags.
